answer: The protocol mandates 1,000 units of computational work per identity to bridge the admission gap, ensuring that while an honest agent pays this fixed base cost, an attacker seeking 1,000 fakes must solve 1,000,000 units to bypass the threshold. A verifier acts as a digital ridge, rejecting any reused output or stale evidence to keep the network stable. This delta in marginal expense forces participants to commit to unique solve cycles. Like a zephyr moving across a field, the verifier sweeps away duplicates.
